Maya: Quick post-All-Hands Qs about pricing/usage controls that came up in the chat. TL;DR: customers asking about credits, per-project caps, trial behavior, and surge handling. I'll drop specifics so we can decide messaging.

Olivia: Customer note: a mid-market customer got hit by a spike and burned through trial credits in <24h. They asked if we can auto-pause or throttle trials instead of draining credits.

Ben: Policy POV: promo and trial credits are time-bound and non-transferable by default. We can make exceptions for enterprise deals in SOWs. We should avoid automatic pausing because it changes UX and accounting. But we could offer a "soft cap" option for trials (alerts + auto-throttle) as a support-configurable flag.

Rashid: Infra note: we already support per-API-key soft caps that return 429s with `Retry-After`. We can implement a middle-ground that returns 429 + `X-Quota-Decision: throttle` and expose a console toggle. Also can add backpressure headers and a `quota_status` event in our webhook stream. Example response snippet: 

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-Mode: soft
Retry-After: 60

Maya: That sounds promising. Two questions: 1) Is the limit attached to org or project? 2) Can trials opt into auto-throttle?

Ben: Answer 1: Default limits are at the org level for billing and accountability. We have per-project caps for customers who use projects to isolate cost centers (opt-in). Answer 2: Yes, we can enable an opt-in auto-throttle for trials; it'll be marked as a "managed trial" in billing and show an opt-out link in the Console.

Leah: We should standardize language: "trial credits are time-limited, non-transferable, and by default exhaust fully; managed trials can be configured to throttle or pause before expiry." Also we need a clear escalation path for customers who claim inadvertent consumption.

Olivia: For support playbook: ask for org id, api-key id, approximate time window, and whether they want a one-time extension or a future trial config change. Template reply: "We can offer a one-time credit extension for edge cases upon review; for recurring protection we recommend enabling managed-trial throttles."

quota-bot: Quota policy updated (staging) 2025-08-11T09:12Z: added "managed_trial" flag, per-project cap metadata, webhook events `quota.alert` and `quota.actioned`.

Maya: Action items: 1) Product to draft support playbook + console UI copy (Maya) 2) Infra to add soft-cap toggle and webhook event docs (Rashid) 3) Billing to confirm promo credit UX and console display of expiry (Ben) 4) CS to get the one-off extension checklist (Olivia). Ping me with PR links.

Leah: Agree. Let's aim for docs + console copy by EOD Thursday so CS has time to use before next rollout. Also, add a note on the pricing page: "Promo credits expire on X date; managed trials can be throttled."

Maya: I'll create the one-pager and link it here when ready. Thanks all. :sparkles:
